To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the single transmembrane Ca(2+ )binding protein, STIm1, is present in pig oocytes.
STIM1, a single transmembrane Ca(2+), binds Ca(2+) in the endoplasmatic reticulum and upon Ca(2+) depletion moves to the cell membrane, where it stimulates the influx of Ca(2+).
STIM1 is a sensor of Ca2+ store content that after depletion moves to the membrane to stimulate Ca2+ entry.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of STIM1 and the regulation of store-operated calcium entry in oocytes.
the molecular mechanism of store-operated calcium entry in the pig.
the role of STIM1 as a sensor and regulator of store-operated calcium entry in the oocytes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
STIM1 is an essential component of the store-operated Ca ^{2+} entry pathway in oocytes.
STIM1 regulates store operated Ca2+ entry.
STIM1 is a Ca(2+), store operated Ca(2+) channel (SOCE) regulator in oocytes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
STIM1 regulates store-depletion induced Ca(2+) release in oocytes.
STIM1 is a key regulator of store-operated calcium entry in oocytes.
STIM1 functions as a Ca2+ sensor that links the ER to the activation of SOCE.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the STIM1 protein is present in pig oocytes and that it plays a role in store-operated calcium entry.
STIM1 is a key player in the regulation of store-operated calcium entry in oocytes.

STIM1 is present in the oocyte cytoplasm where it can be redistributed to the plasma membrane in response to depletion of the Ca(+) stores and that this redistribution results in an enhanced store-operated Ca(+2) current.
